scenes.title: The Red Ribbon
scenes.summary: On Tuesday morning F3 happily recovers her own suitcase while the unclaimed bag stays locked away.
scenes.intro: Tuesday morning arrives bright and clear at the {SHOW}. {F3} hurries downstairs to the front desk, where {F1} and {M1} have her returned suitcase waiting. Listen to the whole scene first.
story: Good morning, Madam {F3}! Look what arrived at our gate last night.
My suitcase! Let me open the top pocket... yes, my red ribbon!
And your teacup inside? Is it still in one piece?
Not a single crack! Who brought it back?
We do not know. Someone left it on the step and rang the bell.
And he did not ask for his own suitcase with the wooden train?
He left a short note asking us to keep it until Friday.
How curious! The handwriting on that tag felt oddly familiar to me.
Really? Do you know someone in {CITY}?
Twenty-five years ago I taught piano near here, though memories fade.
For now, his bag stays safe under lock and key.
Wonderful! Now I am ready for a big breakfast.
scenes.outro: {F3} has her teacup and clothes back, and a twenty-five-year-old memory is starting to stir. Next, trouble brews in the breakfast kitchen. See you next time.

scenes.title: No Milk in the Fridge
scenes.summary: Twenty minutes before breakfast, F2's supplier van breaks down and the kitchen is out of milk and eggs.
scenes.intro: Back in the café kitchen, {F2} opens the fridge and gasps just as {F1} and owner {M2} walk in. Eight guests are waking up upstairs, and breakfast starts in twenty minutes. Listen first.
story: Oh no! {M2}, {F1}, we have a kitchen emergency!
Please do not say the word emergency before my morning coffee!
The dairy van has a flat tyre outside town. Look in the fridge!
One tiny splash of milk, two eggs, and no butter at all!
Eight hungry guests will come down the stairs at seven thirty!
My bread dough is ready in the oven, at least.
Give me a bag and some cash! The corner market opens at seven.
Can you run there and back in ten minutes?
Watch me! Tell me exactly what to buy.
Three bottles of milk, twenty eggs, butter, cheese, and red apples!
Here is fifty from the cash box. Bring back the receipt!
Hold the fort—I am already out the door!
scenes.outro: Armed with a shopping list and cash from the till, {F1} sprints toward the morning market. Let's see what she comes back with next time.

scenes.title: Counting the Change
scenes.summary: F1 returns breathless with two full grocery bags and counts the exact change for M2.
scenes.intro: Nine minutes later, {F1} bursts back through the courtyard gate carrying two heavy cloth bags of groceries for {F2} and {M2}. Listen to the scene in the target language first.
story: Nine minutes! Here are the milk, the eggs, and the apples!
You are a hero, {F1}! Give me the milk first for the coffee machine.
Impressive speed! Did the shopkeeper give you a receipt?
Right here! Everything cost thirty-eight, so here is twelve in change.
Ten, eleven, twelve. Exact to the last coin—thank you!
Wait a second, {F1}... which packet of butter did you grab?
The gold wrapper on the top shelf. Why?
That is extra-salty sea butter! My sweet jam rolls need plain butter!
Oh no! All the wrappers looked the same when I was running!
Can we serve salty butter with sweet strawberry jam?
Wait—salty butter is terrible for jam, but amazing for scrambled eggs!
Phew! Quick thinking saves breakfast again.
scenes.outro: An accidental packet of salted butter nearly caused a jam crisis, until {F2} turned it into the secret ingredient for the eggs. See you next time.

scenes.title: Herbs from the Courtyard
scenes.summary: M1 clips fresh green herbs from his courtyard pot to finish the scrambled eggs right on time.
scenes.intro: In the kitchen, {F2} whisks the eggs while {M1} walks in carrying a small handful of fresh green herbs from the courtyard pot as {F1} sets the four tables. Listen first.
story: I heard shouting about butter from all the way out in the courtyard.
{F1} bought sea-salt butter, so today we are making French-style eggs!
Good. Put these fresh green herbs on top before you serve them.
Did you grow those herbs yourself, {M1}?
Somebody has to take care of the courtyard plants.
Smell that! Warm bread, hot eggs, and fresh herbs.
Where do the small spoons and napkins go?
Put one napkin and one small spoon beside every blue cup.
Seven twenty-nine on my watch. Guests are coming down the stairs.
Four tables, eight chairs, everything in place!
Pour the hot water into the teapot, {F1}, here they come!
Not bad for day two, rookie.
scenes.outro: With one minute to spare, the four café tables are set and smelling of fresh bread and courtyard herbs. Next time, the guests sit down to eat.

scenes.title: Juice on the Tie
scenes.summary: F3 enjoys her tea without sugar while M2 tries to impress the room and spills orange juice on his silk tie.
scenes.intro: Breakfast is in full swing in the sunlit café corner. {F3} sits by the window while {M2} insists on helping {F1} serve the drinks like a grand hotel host. Listen first.
story: Good morning again, Madam {F3}! Would you like coffee or black tea?
Black tea without sugar, please, and one slice of warm bread.
Allow me to pour the fresh orange juice, madam!
Oh, how kind of you, sir. Just half a glass.
At our guesthouse, five-star service comes naturally—whoops!
Careful, {M2}, the pitcher spout is wide!
Oh dear! Not a drop on the table, thank goodness... all of it is on my tie!
Do not worry! Cold sparkling water takes orange juice right out.
Here is a clean cloth and cold water, {M2}.
Excuse me, madam, I shall retreat to my office with dignity!
Your scrambled eggs are delicious, {F1}. Tell {F2} my compliments!
scenes.outro: {F3} loved her breakfast, even if {M2}'s tie drank most of the orange juice. Soon the front-desk telephone brings news about the mystery suitcase. See you next time.

scenes.title: The Friday Caller
scenes.summary: A nervous male caller phones the front desk to check on the blue suitcase and hangs up without giving his name.
scenes.intro: After breakfast, the lobby is quiet again while {F1} updates the paper ledger and {M1} oils the front door hinge. Suddenly the desk telephone rings. Let's listen in.
story: Who is it? Another booking for the weekend?
Wait—hello, sir! You are calling about the dark-blue suitcase?
Ask him his name! Write it down!
Yes, sir, we locked your bag safely in our closet. What is your name, please?
What is he saying? Why are you frowning?
Sir? He says, 'Please do not open the white paper parcel. I will come Friday at noon.'
Give me the phone—let me ask him properly!
Too late! He said 'Thank you' and hung up!
Quiet, polite, maybe thirty-five. He sounded nervous, not angry.
Nervous about a wooden toy train? This story gets stranger every hour.
scenes.outro: Now they have an exact appointment—Friday at noon—and a nervous voice on the phone who refuses to give his name. See you next time.

scenes.title: How Regulars Order
scenes.summary: During the quiet afternoon lull, F2 teaches F1 the cafe orders while M1 fixes a wobbly chair.
scenes.intro: In the calm afternoon sunshine, {F1} takes a ten-minute break in the café corner while {F2} wipes the counter and {M1} tightens a loose wooden chair leg. Listen first.
story: Sit down, {F1}! You ran half the city this morning—drink some coffee.
Gladly! With milk and a little sugar, please.
Watch that corner chair—wait ten seconds while I tighten this screw.
Done already? You carry a screwdriver everywhere, {M1}!
Old houses loosen one screw every Tuesday. Now sit.
Look, you survived the breakfast rush and the mystery phone call!
Honestly, I like it here much better than my old grey office.
Wait until Friday at noon—I want a front-row seat when Suitcase Man walks in!
Nobody stares at guests. We hand over the bag and mind our business.
Listen to him! {M1} is twice as curious as we are!
I am simply checking security. That is my job.
Sure, {M1}—your secret is safe with us!
scenes.outro: A quiet cup of coffee, a tightened chair, and three colleagues who are already starting to feel like a team. One scene left in Episode 2—and {M2} is about to make a discovery. See you next time.

scenes.title: Two Names, One Room
scenes.summary: Checking the evening ledger, M2 turns pale: he booked two separate guests into Room 7 on a sold-out night.
scenes.intro: On Wednesday evening, as dusk settles over {CITY}, {M2} comes out of his office holding both the tablet computer and {M1}'s paper ledger, looking pale. {F1} and {M1} look up at once. Listen first.
story: {M1}... {F1}... please tell me room six is free tonight.
No, {M2}, the couple from the south checked into room six an hour ago.
Every key from one to seven is taken, and room eight has wet paint.
Oh, disaster! Yesterday I took a phone booking on the tablet without my glasses!
Wait—let me look at the tablet screen and the paper book together.
Let me guess. You promised somebody a room we do not have?
{M2}! Room seven is already occupied, and you booked a second guest into room seven!
And he arrives on the eight o'clock evening train—in forty minutes!
Told you that tablet is a trap.
It is raining outside and every hotel on our street is full! What do we do?
Wait—what is on the third floor above the stairs?
The old sunny attic study... follow me, quickly!
scenes.outro: Two guests booked into Room 7, pouring rain outside, and only forty minutes before the eight o'clock arrival! Episode 2 is done—join us in Episode 3 to see if the attic can save the night.
